title: Proteus Diagnostic
description: The Proteus diagnostic chamber for detecting AI theatre, automation fog, prompt worship, data mysticism, agentic overclaiming, fake intelligence, and expensive confusion wearing a login screen.

intro.title: AI theatre exposure scan
intro.body: Proteus has opened the AI claim with gloves and a long sigh. This chamber is not anti-AI. It is anti-bullshit wearing AI perfume. Answer carefully; the gradient is already nervous.

questions.question: What does “AI-powered” prove by itself?

answers.text: The product is intelligent.
The workflow is clear.
Someone used a fashionable adjective.
The future has arrived wearing a gradient.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. “AI-powered” proves an adjective has been deployed. Further evidence is required.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Comfortable answer detected. Proteus has placed it beside the pitch deck and stepped back slowly.
questions.realityCheck: AI can be useful, but the label alone says nothing about the task, workflow, risk, error rate, output quality, or business value.
questions.practicalMove: Ask: “What exactly does the AI do, what improves, how is it measured, and what happens when it is wrong?”

questions.question: What is the most dangerous thing about adding AI to a confused process?

answers.text: It becomes too intelligent.
It becomes too expensive.
It automates confusion faster.
It asks to attend meetings.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. Automation is not a priest. It does not bless the mess before multiplying it.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. The mess remains a mess, only now it has throughput and a vendor invoice.
questions.realityCheck: AI can accelerate clear work. It can also industrialise unclear work, bad inputs, weak decisions, and broken handoffs.
questions.practicalMove: Before adding AI, write the process in plain human steps: task, input, output, decision, reviewer, risk, and stop condition. If that list is fog, do not automate it yet.

questions.question: Before buying or building an AI tool, what should be named first?

answers.text: The model.
The task, input, output, risk, and human reviewer.
The logo.
The inspirational launch post.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. The logo can wait in the corridor with the launch post and its emotional gradient.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Incorrect. Proteus has detected procurement theatre forming around an unnamed task.
questions.realityCheck: A tool cannot be judged until the task, input, output, risk, review point, and success measure are clear.
questions.practicalMove: Write one sentence: “This AI will take this input, perform this task, produce this output, be reviewed by this person, and fail safely in this way.”

questions.question: What is prompt worship?

answers.text: Writing clear instructions.
Believing the magic words can rescue an unclear task.
Using examples to guide output.
Calling a prompt a strategy because the font was serious.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. A prompt is not a business process with incense.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. Proteus has detected a small altar forming near the text box.
questions.realityCheck: Prompts help when the task is clear. They cannot replace domain judgement, workflow design, data quality, review criteria, or accountability.
questions.practicalMove: Before improving the prompt, improve the task definition: audience, purpose, source material, constraints, evaluation criteria, and human reviewer.

questions.question: What happens when weak data enters a confident AI system?

answers.text: The system becomes wiser.
The data is purified by innovation.
The mess may return wearing better grammar.
The dashboard starts glowing.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. Bad data with good grammar is still bad data, only now it sounds employable.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. Proteus has detected data mysticism and a suspicious glow near the spreadsheet.
questions.realityCheck: AI outputs inherit the quality, bias, gaps, and ambiguity of the inputs. Fluency can hide bad source material extremely well.
questions.practicalMove: Check data source, freshness, completeness, bias, duplicates, missing fields, and known failure cases before trusting the output.

questions.question: What is the safest response to a confident AI answer in a high-stakes task?

answers.text: Admire the confidence.
Paste it directly into reality.
Verify against reliable sources and known rules.
Ask it to sound more authoritative.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. Confidence is not evidence. It is merely posture with punctuation.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Incorrect. The answer may be fluent, wrong, and already wearing a tie.
questions.realityCheck: AI systems can produce plausible errors. Fluency lowers suspicion, which makes verification more important, not less.
questions.practicalMove: Define which outputs require verification, what source verifies them, who reviews them, and what risk level blocks use.

questions.question: What should trigger caution when someone says the AI agent will handle it?

answers.text: The word agent.
No clear boundary, permission, stop condition, or human escalation.
The demo has a progress bar.
It uses the word autonomous with a straight face.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. A model is not a manager. It should not be left alone with the steering wheel and a quarterly budget.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. Proteus has found autonomy fog and a small liability hiding under the roadmap.
questions.realityCheck: Agentic systems are risky when scope, permissions, failure modes, escalation rules, and accountability are undefined.
questions.practicalMove: Define the agent boundary: what it may do, what it may never do, when it stops, when it asks, and who owns the result.

questions.question: When should AI not replace human judgement?

answers.text: When consequences are serious and context matters.
When humans are bored.
When the output sounds very polished.
When the vendor says trust the system.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. Delegation is not abandonment with a nicer interface.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Incorrect. Proteus has detected judgement outsourcing and a faint smell of liability.
questions.realityCheck: AI can support judgement, but high-stakes, context-heavy, ethical, legal, financial, medical, or reputational decisions require accountable human review.
questions.practicalMove: Classify decisions by risk. For high-risk outputs, require human review, source checking, documented reasoning, and a clear owner.

questions.question: What is pseudo-intelligence in an AI dashboard?

answers.text: A useful signal connected to a decision.
A metric that looks clever but changes nothing.
A chart with tasteful colours.
A prediction that has met reality.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. The chart has achieved decorative intelligence.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. The dashboard is glowing, but the decision is still missing.
questions.realityCheck: Metrics, scores, and predictions are useful only when they connect to decisions, thresholds, actions, and verification.
questions.practicalMove: For every AI score or dashboard signal, write the decision it changes, the threshold for action, and the review method.

questions.question: When is AI probably a business model costume?

answers.text: When it improves a known task with measured results.
When the product is ordinary but the pitch says autonomous intelligence five times.
When users understand the workflow.
When error handling is boring and clear.

questions.defaultCorrectReaction: Correct. The business model has arrived wearing an AI cape and asking for a valuation.
questions.defaultWrongReaction: Not quite. Proteus has found an ordinary workflow inside a theatrical costume.
questions.realityCheck: AI is not a business model by itself. Value comes from solving a real problem with a clear workflow, buyer, cost structure, and measurable improvement.
questions.practicalMove: Ask: “What customer problem exists without the AI language, what changes for the user, and why would anyone pay after the novelty expires?”

diagnoses.title: AI Theatre Exposure
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: The claim may contain more spectacle than mechanism. Proteus has checked behind the curtain and found adjectives nesting.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that AI language is being used to inflate perceived value, hide weak workflow thinking, or make ordinary automation sound like a visiting deity.
diagnoses.realMechanism: AI theatre works because novelty, fear, and technical vagueness create temporary authority. People stop asking what the system actually does because the demo has sparkles.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Ask: “What does the system do, what input does it need, what output does it produce, how is it checked, and what specific result improves?”
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free warning card: AI Theatre Warning Card can help identify claims where the adjective is doing more work than the system.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full detector: The AI Theatre Detector goes deeper into pitch fog, fake intelligence, and business claims wearing AI perfume.
diagnoses.shareLine: AI theatre begins when the vocabulary grows faster than the use case.

diagnoses.title: Automation Before Thought
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: You may be trying to automate a process that has not yet earned the dignity of being understood.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that automation is being added before the task, workflow, handoffs, exceptions, and ownership are clear.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Automation amplifies whatever already exists. If the process is fog, automation produces faster fog with better uptime.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Before adding AI, write the process in plain human steps: task, input, output, decision, reviewer, risk, and stop condition. If that list is fog, do not automate it yet.
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free warning card: AI Theatre Warning Card can help catch automation fever before it multiplies the mess.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full detector: The AI Theatre Detector helps inspect processes before someone adds a bot and calls it transformation.
diagnoses.shareLine: Automation is not a priest. It does not bless the mess before multiplying it.

diagnoses.title: Prompt-Worship Irritation
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: A prompt may have been promoted beyond its competence. Proteus has removed the incense.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that prompt quality is being treated as a substitute for task clarity, domain knowledge, workflow design, or review criteria.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Prompt worship is attractive because it turns a systems problem into a sentence problem. That feels cheaper until reality returns with invoices.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Before improving the prompt, define the task, source material, output standard, audience, constraints, examples, failure modes, and review method.
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free warning card: AI Theatre Warning Card can help distinguish useful prompting from text-box religion.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full detector: The AI Theatre Detector examines when prompts help and when they become decorative control panels.
diagnoses.shareLine: A prompt is not a process. It is an instruction looking for adult supervision.

diagnoses.title: Data Mysticism
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: The data may be glowing because nobody has checked whether it is clean, complete, current, or meaningful.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that data is being treated as automatically authoritative because it is numerical, technical, or inconvenient to inspect.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Data mysticism works because numbers feel objective even when the collection process, definitions, gaps, bias, duplicates, and context are a compost heap.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Check source, definition, age, missing fields, duplication, bias, collection method, and known failure cases before asking AI to make it sound clever.
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free warning card: AI Theatre Warning Card helps identify data mysticism before it receives a dashboard.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full detector: The AI Theatre Detector includes sharper checks for data quality, fake certainty, and metric theatre.
diagnoses.shareLine: Bad data with good grammar is still bad data, only now it sounds employable.

diagnoses.title: Agentic Fog Event
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: An agent has been mentioned without boundaries. Proteus has hidden the steering wheel.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that autonomy claims are being made without clear permissions, limits, escalation rules, stop conditions, or accountability.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Agentic fog appears when people confuse multi-step automation with judgement, responsibility, or safe delegation.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Define what the agent may do, what it may never do, what it can spend or change, when it must stop, when it must ask, and who owns the result.
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free warning card: AI Theatre Warning Card can help spot agent claims that need a leash, a map, and an adult.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full detector: The AI Theatre Detector examines agentic claims before the bot wanders into operations wearing confidence.
diagnoses.shareLine: A model is not a manager. Do not leave it alone with the steering wheel and a quarterly budget.

diagnoses.title: Business Model Costume Alert
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: The business model may be ordinary, but it has put on an AI cape and is asking to be treated as destiny.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that AI is being used to decorate positioning rather than solve a real customer problem with measurable value.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Business model costumes work because the market rewards novelty signals until buyers ask what the product actually changes.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Strip the AI language away. Ask what customer problem remains, who pays, what improves, what cost is removed, and why the user returns after curiosity fades.
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free warning card: AI Theatre Warning Card helps detect when the business model is mostly costume.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full detector: The AI Theatre Detector goes deeper into AI-wrapped offers, fake differentiation, and novelty inflation.
diagnoses.shareLine: A chatbot placed near a business problem does not automatically become a strategy.

diagnoses.title: Workflow Fog
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: The workflow may be missing, unclear, or hiding behind enthusiasm. Proteus has requested a map and received vibes.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that the actual human process is not understood well enough to automate, improve, or delegate safely.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Workflow fog survives because teams talk about tools before naming the work, the handoffs, the exception cases, and the boring parts where failure breeds.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Map the current workflow with steps, inputs, outputs, decisions, exceptions, owners, tools, delays, and failure points before choosing AI.
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free warning card: AI Theatre Warning Card can help reveal whether the workflow exists or is merely implied by slides.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full detector: The AI Theatre Detector helps expose workflow fog before technology makes it expensive.
diagnoses.shareLine: If the human workflow is fog, AI will industrialise the fog.

diagnoses.title: Human Review Gap
diagnoses.proteusVerdict: The system may produce outputs nobody is properly responsible for checking. A liability has put on soft shoes.
diagnoses.whatItMeans: This diagnosis suggests that review, verification, escalation, and ownership are missing or too vague for the risk level involved.
diagnoses.realMechanism: Human review gaps appear when organisations want speed from AI but quietly hope accountability will remain theoretical.
diagnoses.practicalMove: Classify output risk. Define who reviews it, what they check, what source verifies it, what errors block use, and who owns the final decision.
diagnoses.freeAntidoteCopy: Free warning card: AI Theatre Warning Card can help catch review gaps before polished errors escape.
diagnoses.paidAntidoteCopy: Full detector: The AI Theatre Detector examines human review, verification, and accountability before the system starts sounding sure.
diagnoses.shareLine: Fluent output without review is just confidence looking for a victim.
